Name: Augustine of Hippo
Summary: North African bishop whose writings shaped Western Christianity for a thousand years. Converted from a life of ambition and sin after years of restless searching, he became the church's great teacher on grace, sin, and the city of God.
Contribution: Gave the church its classic doctrine of grace and original sin, defended the faith against Pelagianism and Donatism, and modeled honest confession.
KeyWorks: Confessions; The City of God; On Christian Doctrine
Testimony: His testimony - 'You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our hearts are restless until they rest in you' - turned a sinner's story into the church's prayer book.
